analyst_view.overall: Albacete are 20th, one point from safety, after five straight wins ended with a 1-0 loss at Burgos (a Carlos Neva own goal). They get José Corpas back from a three-match ban, but Antonio Puertas (knee, recovering slower than expected according to coach Joseba Etxeberria), Samu Obeng and others stay out, which their recent games already reflect. Tenerife are 13th and have drawn four of their last five, most recently 0-0 with Mallorca; they have taken six points from 18 away. It is an emotional trip for Tenerife after the death of forward Jesús de Miguel on 4 November; Albacete have left it to Tenerife whether there is a tribute before kick-off. No referee is named yet; the view nudges Albacete's attack up slightly for Corpas and otherwise stays on the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Albacete get Corpas back from his ban, a return the numbers have not moved for, so I nudge it to about 2.35. Tenerife's run of draws and low scoring is already counted and keeps the lean small.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners and already add for Albacete's heavy recent corner count (43 in six games, momentum +5%). Corpas' return on the wing fits that pattern rather than changing it, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.3 cards and already add a lot for both sides' recent card counts (momentum +15% and +17%). Yesterday I leaned slightly lower for the emotional context of Tenerife's first trip since Jesús de Miguel's death, but the tribute is still undecided and Albacete's relegation fight cuts the other way, so I drop that hunch and stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, with Albacete's recent volume already counted (+4% momentum). Corpas back adds an attacking option the numbers did not have during his ban, so I nudge it to about 24.7. Tenerife's low attempt count of late (58 in six) is already in the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.1 shots on target and already trim both sides for poor recent accuracy. Albacete still miss Puertas and Obeng and Tenerife have scored little; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 7.1.
